ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Ammonia (NH$_3$) and nitrous oxide (N$_2$O) undergo the following reaction: $$2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + 3\text{N}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 4\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g})$$ The enthalpy values of various bonds are known: the N-H bond enthalpy is $388\text{kJ/mol}$; the N-O bond enthalpy is $210\text{kJ/mol}$; the N=O bond enthalpy is $630\text{kJ/mol}$; the N≡N bond enthalpy is $941\text{kJ/mol}$; the O-H bond enthalpy is $463\text{kJ/mol}$. If 25.00 grams of NH$_3$ and 25.00 grams of N$_2$O react completely, what is the magnitude of the energy change?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Ammonia (NH$_3$) and nitrous oxide (N$_2$O) undergo the following reaction: $$2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + 3\text{N}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 4\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g})$$ The enthalpy values of various bonds are known: the N-H bond enthalpy is $388\text{kJ/mol}$; the N-O bond enthalpy is $210\text{kJ/mol}$; the N=O bond enthalpy is $630\text{kJ/mol}$; the N≡N bond enthalpy is $941\text{kJ/mol}$; the O-H bond enthalpy is $463\text{kJ/mol}$. If 25.00 grams of NH$_3$ and 25.00 grams of N$_2$O react completely, what is the magnitude of the energy change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached figure shows a thermodynamic data table, listing the standard entropies S° of NH3(g), N2O(g), N2(g), H2O(g), with values respectively 193, 220, 192, 189 J/mol·K. The standard entropy data in this image have no direct use for the bond enthalpy calculation required by the specified method in this problem. Then reason: The balanced reaction given in the problem is 2NH3(g) + 3N2O(g) → 4N2(g) + 3H2O(g). According to the specified method, first calculate the amounts of substance: n(NH3)=25.00/17.03≈1.468 mol; n(N2O)=25.00/44.01≈0.568 mol. Compare n/stoichiometric coefficient: for NH3 it is 1.468/2≈0.734, for N2O it is 0.568/3≈0.189, therefore N2O is the limiting reactant, and the reaction extent ξ≈n(N2O)/3≈0.189 mol. The bond enthalpy change for each stoichiometric reaction packet: bonds broken include 6 N-H bonds in 2 NH3, and, according to the specified method, 6 N=O bonds taken in 3 N2O; bonds formed include 4 N≡N bonds and 6 O-H bonds in 3 H2O. Therefore ΔH_packet=[6(388)+6(630)]-[4(941)+6(463)] kJ = (2328+3780)-(3764+2778) kJ = 6108-6542 = -434 kJ. The magnitude of the energy change is |ΔH_packet|×ξ≈434×0.189≈82.16 kJ.

method.method_draft: Read the balanced reaction from the text: 2 NH3 + 3 N2O → 4 N2 + 3 H2O. Compute moles from the given masses: n(NH3)=25.00/17.03 and n(N2O)=25.00/44.01. Compare n/stoichiometric coefficient to find N2O is limiting, so the reaction extent is ξ=n(N2O)/3. Compute the enthalpy for one stoichiometric reaction packet: bonds broken = 2×3×D(N-H)+3×2×D(N=O); bonds formed = 4×D(N≡N)+3×2×D(O-H). Thus ΔH_packet=[6(388)+6(630)]−[4(941)+6(463)] kJ. Multiply |ΔH_packet| by ξ to obtain the magnitude, about 82.16 kJ.
